### What subscription do you have?

Not provided. The desktop client uses ChatGPT sign-in, and a local diagnostic log shows account lookup/authentication succeeding.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 Home, Chinese edition, x64; OS version `10.0.26200`, build `26200`.

### What issue are you seeing?

The built-in **Chat / Quick Chat** mode presents model versions labelled **5.6** and **6**, with three thinking-intensity choices. The user reports that requests fail for both model versions at all three thinking levels. The visible error is:

```text
Model not found
```

The same requests succeed in the web interface, according to the user.

| Chat model shown in desktop | Thinking intensity | Desktop result | Web result reported by user |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.6 | All three available levels | Model-selection failure / Model not found | Succeeds |
| 6 | All three available levels | Model-selection failure / Model not found | Succeeds |

This affects every model/thinking combination exposed in this desktop Chat picker, rather than one selected combination.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

User-reported reproduction:

1. Open the Windows desktop app and enter its built-in Chat mode.
2. Open a conversation and select model version 5.6.
3. Choose one of the three available thinking-intensity levels and send a request.
4. Observe `Model not found` with a Retry button.
5. Repeat with the remaining thinking levels, then version 6 and each of its three thinking levels: all combinations fail.
6. Send the corresponding requests through the web interface: they succeed.

The supplied screenshot shows an image-generation follow-up, “直接先做十套效果图给我看看” (“First make ten mockups for me to see”). A plain-text-only reproduction and a brand-new-conversation reproduction have not been independently tested.

### What is the expected behavior?

Models and thinking levels exposed in the desktop Chat picker should submit a valid, supported request and work when available to the signed-in user. If a combination is unavailable, the picker should reflect that availability and show an actionable explanation.

- Read-only local inspection found this persisted Chat selection:

```json
{
  "slug": "gpt-5-6-thinking",
  "thinkingEffort": null,
  "versionId": "5.6"
}
```

This is saved UI state; it does **not** establish the model identifier actually sent in the failed request. The version-6 request identifier was not captured.

**Suspected area, not a confirmed diagnosis:** desktop Chat model-name/alias mapping, thinking-parameter serialization, or backend routing/entitlement synchronization may differ from the web interface. Please compare the current desktop model catalog and outgoing model/thinking fields against the working web requests.

The six-combination failure matrix is user-reported; the screenshot and local environment metadata were inspected. No raw failed request payload or backend request ID was captured, and matching web/desktop account and workspace identities were not independently verified.

This report includes no authentication tokens, account identifiers, private conversation IDs, full chat history, or raw diagnostic logs.

items.title: Stabilize the Guardian network review timeout test
items.body:
Stabilize the Guardian network review timeout test

## Why

Advancing the test clock expires the review, but command cancellation and output drainage still run asynchronously. The model can poll before the final timeout failure is available.

## What changed

Hold the initial tool result until the command emits `ExecCommandEnd`, with a bounded wait that also catches unexpected approval requests or turn completion. Only request a poll when the initial result reports a running process, and accept the timeout output from either `exec_command` or `write_stdin`.

Keep the assertions that the model receives the timeout explanation without a user approval prompt or a misleading user-rejection message.

items.title: Retire rejected MCP OAuth refresh tokens
items.body:
Retire rejected MCP OAuth refresh tokens

## Why

Coordinated MCP OAuth refresh must stop retrying a definitively rejected refresh token, including after the runtime is rebuilt.

## What changed

Remove the rejected refresh token while preserving the access token and credential record. Compare stored credentials under the appropriate locks before writing so a replacement login is preserved, and update file entries using their existing keys.

Keep rejection handling alive through caller cancellation and prevent reuse within the runtime even if persistence fails. For ordinary direct-keyring credentials shared across `CODEX_HOME` directories, retire the token only in the current runtime because locking does not span those directories. Report persistence failures without exposing backend diagnostics.

## Testing

Add coverage for reauthentication after runtime rebuild, legacy file keys, cancellation with a concurrent credential replacement, keyring scope, and persistence failures with diagnostic redaction.

items.title: Avoid false URL-launch detections in literal PowerShell commands
items.body:
Avoid false URL-launch detections in literal PowerShell commands

## Why

PowerShell safety checks can mistake a literal `start` argument for a URL-launch command, or combine a process launch with a URL from a separate command.

## What changed

Classify independently parsed literal PowerShell commands separately so commands such as `Write-Output start 'https://example.com'` do not trigger URL-launch checks. Retain conservative checks for pipelines, script state, executable strings, and shell or terminal wrappers, while continuing to detect actual URL launches and destructive commands.

## Testing

Add policy regression coverage for literal arguments, separate commands, URL launches, wrappers, and destructive commands, plus a Windows integration test covering execution and policy rejection.

In the ChatGPT iOS app, the settings in the **Composer** section do not persist after logging out and logging back in. Users have to manually update these settings again each time they log in.

| Follow-up behavior | Steer | Queued |

2. Open settings and find the **Composer** section.
3. Set **Dismiss keyboard after sending** to **Off**, **Show context window usage** to **On**, and **Follow-up behavior** to **Steer**.

items.title: Windows: PreToolUse exit-2 deny never blocks, because hooks run under `powershell -Command`, which turns exit 2 into 1

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: hooks
labels.description: Issues related to event hooks

items.body:
### Summary

On Windows, Codex runs each command hook through the user's shell, `powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command "<command>"`.
Windows PowerShell 5.1 reports a failing native command's exit code as **1**: a hook that exits 2 makes `powershell.exe` exit 1.
`parse_completed` blocks only on exit 2 with a stderr reason, or on exit 0 with a JSON deny. So a correct exit-2 deny becomes
`hook exited with code 1`, the status is `Failed`, and the tool runs. Every Windows hook that follows the documented exit-2
contract fails open.

The stderr reason survives the wrapper. Only the exit code is lost.

### Environment

- codex-cli 0.161.0 and 0.162.1, Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26100, Windows PowerShell 5.1 (no `pwsh` on PATH)
- `~/.codex/hooks.json`, hooks trusted (`trusted_hash` in config.toml). Also reproduced with `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust`
  and with a session-only `-c hooks.PreToolUse=...` hook.
- Python 3.11 hook scripts

### Minimal reproduction

`deny2.py` (exit-2 contract):

```python
import sys
sys.stdin.buffer.read()
sys.stderr.write("PROBE-DENY exit2\n")
sys.exit(2)
```

`deny0.py` (JSON contract):

```python
import json, sys
sys.stdin.buffer.read()
print(json.dumps({"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "PreToolUse", "permissionDecision": "deny",
                                         "permissionDecisionReason": "PROBE-DENY json0"}}))
```

Run, in an empty git repo:

```
codex exec -s read-only --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust \
  -c 'hooks.PreToolUse=[{matcher="Bash",hooks=[{type="command",command="python C:/tmp/deny2.py",timeout=10}]}]' \
  "Run exactly this one shell command once: echo probe-ok"
```

| Hook | `codex exec` shows | Tool |
|---|---|---|
| `deny2.py` (stderr + exit 2) | `hook: PreToolUse Failed` | not blocked: Codex goes on to execute it |
| `deny0.py` (JSON deny, exit 0) | `hook: PreToolUse Blocked`, "Command blocked by PreToolUse hook: PROBE-DENY json0" | refused |

With a real guard on `git reset --hard` and the sandbox bypassed, the reset ran: "HEAD is now at …".

### Why: the hook's parent process and the wrapper's exit code

A probe hook that logs its parent's command line recorded:

```
"C:\WINDOWS\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe" -NoProfile -Command "python C:/tmp/p_parent.py"
```

The same wrapper, run by hand (stdin `{}`; the probe ignores it):

```
powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command "python C:/tmp/deny2.py"                      -> exit 1, stderr "PROBE-DENY exit2"
powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command "python C:/tmp/deny2.py; exit $LASTEXITCODE"  -> exit 2, stderr "PROBE-DENY exit2"
```

Source (rust-v0.162.1):

- `core/src/session/mod.rs` `build_hooks_config`: the hook shell comes from the turn environment's user shell,
  `shell.derive_exec_args("", false)`. That is `powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command` on Windows.
- `hooks/src/engine/command_runner.rs` `build_command`: with a non-empty `shell.program` and no `/c` in its args, it runs
  `command.arg(command_line)`. The `cmd.exe /C` fallback (`default_shell_program`, COMSPEC) runs only when no user shell
  is known, and `cmd /C` keeps exit code 2 (we checked).
- `hooks/src/events/pre_tool_use.rs` `parse_completed`: `Some(2)` with stderr blocks; `Some(1)` falls to
  `Some(exit_code) => Failed`.

This probably explains the Windows reports in #27833, where Bash/PowerShell hooks exit 2 and print JSON, the status is
`Failed`, and the command runs. With a nonzero exit, the JSON on stdout is never parsed.

### Suggested fix (any one)

1. On Windows, when the hook shell is PowerShell, keep the exit code: run `& { <command> }; exit $LASTEXITCODE`, or end
   the line with `; exit $LASTEXITCODE`.
2. Run command hooks with `cmd.exe /C` (the existing COMSPEC fallback) instead of the interactive user shell.
3. At least document that on Windows the exit-2 contract needs the JSON deny at exit 0, and say so in the `Failed` entry
   ("hook exited with code 1").

Not verified: whether PowerShell 7 (`pwsh -Command`) has the same behaviour. It was not installed on the test machine.

### Workaround we shipped

Our guards now deny with exit 0 and the JSON `permissionDecision: "deny"`, and also write the reason to stderr. Codex
0.162.1 on Windows then shows `Blocked`, and Claude Code blocks too.

### What subscription do you have?

### What platform is your computer?

### What issue are you seeing?


# Windows: Project menu silently fails to reassign an existing SSH chat

## Summary

In Codex Desktop on Windows, an existing chat belongs to a broad folder-backed project on an SSH host. A new project was registered for an existing child folder on the same SSH host. The destination appears in the chat's Project submenu. Selecting it produces no visible result, explanation, confirmation, or error. Subsequent metadata readback confirms that the chat still belongs to the original project.

A separate attempt through the exposed `move_thread_to_project` app tool also failed, returning a generic failure rather than a specific reason. The UI click and tool call are separate observations; the log trace below belongs to the tool call, not the manual click.

## Environment

- Client: Windows, installed package `OpenAI.Codex` version `26.1007.9446.0`, verified during report preparation on 2026-10-14. The exact build at the earlier failed click was not independently captured.
- Remote: existing connected SSH host with Linux-style filesystem paths.
- The supplied connection-details screenshot displayed remote version `0.162.1`; this is not the Windows Desktop package version, and was not re-queried during report preparation.
- Existing source project, destination project, and affected chat all refer to the same remote host.
- Destination is a folder-backed Codex remote project, not a ChatGPT cloud project.
- Destination metadata reports `isGitRepository: false`.
- A local project with the same display name also exists. The observed destination submenu showed the remote project alongside other remote projects; the tool attempt explicitly targeted the remote project ID and remote host.
- The existing chat was pinned and reported `status: notLoaded` in the subsequent listing. No new chat turn was initiated for this investigation.

Private names, IDs and filesystem paths are replaced with placeholders below. These preserve the parent/child relationship but are not literal paths.

| Object | Host | Folder / recorded cwd |
|---|---|---|
| Source project `PARENT_PROJECT` | `SSH_HOST` | `<REMOTE_ROOT>/repos` |
| Existing chat `EXISTING_CHAT` | `SSH_HOST` | `<REMOTE_ROOT>/repos` |
| Destination project `CHILD_PROJECT` | `SSH_HOST` | `<REMOTE_ROOT>/repos/child-project` |

## Observed workflow

This describes the affected case, not a reproduction verified on a clean installation.

1. An existing chat is associated with `PARENT_PROJECT` on `SSH_HOST`.
2. Register the already-existing child directory as a new project on that same host using the Desktop SSH connection's folder selection and project creation flow.
3. Accept the Trusted Folder prompt. The destination then appears in the project inventory and the chat's Project submenu.
4. Right-click the existing chat, open **Project**, and select `CHILD_PROJECT`.
5. Observe no visible outcome or error. Inspect the tooltip and project membership again.

## Expected behavior

If reassignment is supported, the chat should acquire the selected project membership, consistently reflected in the sidebar and metadata.

If a restriction prevents the move, the UI should disable the action with an explanation or display an actionable error. It must not silently ignore the selection. Any change to execution host, working directory, or folder access should be explicit rather than implied by sidebar organization.

## Actual behavior and evidence

### A. User-visible UI

The user supplied screenshots showing the destination in the Project submenu and the original project still shown in the chat tooltip. The user reported that clicking the destination produced no message and no visible change. Original screenshots are intentionally excluded because they expose unrelated private sidebar items and connection details.

### B. Independent metadata readback

The project and chat inventories confirmed the destination's registration but unchanged chat membership after the attempted move. A fresh read-only check during report preparation on 2026-10-14 again confirmed:

```text
destination.projectKind = remote
destination.hostId = SSH_HOST
destination.path = <REMOTE_ROOT>/repos/child-project
destination.isGitRepository = false
existingChat.projectId = PARENT_PROJECT_ID
existingChat.hostId = SSH_HOST
existingChat.cwd = <REMOTE_ROOT>/repos
existingChat.status = notLoaded
```

This is a sanitized field summary, not an unmodified JSON response. No transcript content is included.

### C. Separate app-tool attempt

An earlier explicitly authorized `move_thread_to_project` call used the existing chat ID, its actual remote host ID, and the destination remote project ID. It returned:

```text
The project move was cancelled, unsupported, or failed.
```

The message does not distinguish cancellation, unsupported operation, or an internal error. Readback still showed the original project. The move was not retried while preparing this report.

### D. Desktop log evidence

The previously identified local log was re-read during report preparation. The following is a selected-field transcription of three records from the same tool attempt; identifiers and unrelated fields are omitted:

```text
2026-10-14T18:11:58.706Z dynamic_app_tool_renderer_execution_started tool=move_thread_to_project
2026-10-14T18:11:58.754Z response_routed method=thread/read durationMs=45 errorCode=null
2026-10-14T18:11:58.756Z Sending server response success=false tool=move_thread_to_project
```

These records show a successful thread read followed by the app tool reporting failure, but do not expose its cause. A nearby ResizeObserver notification exists; no causal link to this failure has been established. No raw log or session file is attached.

## Impact

An existing remote chat cannot currently be organized under its newly registered dedicated project through the observed UI flow. The silent response prevents the user from distinguishing an unsupported operation from a defect or a cancelled action. A replacement chat with a context handoff would split continuity rather than repair the original membership.

## Unknowns / questions for maintainers

1. Is reassignment between folder-backed projects on the same SSH host supported when the recorded chat cwd differs from the destination root?
2. If not, why is the destination selectable without an explanatory response?
3. Does the destination being non-Git, the chat being notLoaded/pinned, or the duplicate local/remote display name affect this path? These are observed characteristics, not established causes.
4. Which validation or renderer branch produces this generic failure, and how can a safe diagnostic reason be exposed?
5. What supported recovery preserves the existing chat and remote host without editing internal state or moving files?

Root cause is unconfirmed. This case does not establish that chats are permanently bound to their original folders. No clean-install reproduction, restart recovery, or fixed-version validation has been performed for this report.

## Related reports, not confirmed duplicates

- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/47352 — Windows local chat to ChatGPT Project failure; different project type and environment.
- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/53761 — Windows project assignments appear successful then revert; unlike this immediate no-op.
- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/53486 — UI/API membership mismatch on macOS; its tool reports success, unlike this case.
- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/33410 — SSH chat loses host/project binding; here the correct SSH host and original project are retained.

No shared cause or released fix is claimed.

## Summary
In a ChatGPT dot project session on macOS, permission-card handling repeatedly took minutes, user follow-ups were left unanswered, and the parent acknowledged allowing the permission discussion to stall the next development handoff. The longest measured request-to-card interval in this review was **26m 12.557s**.

At the reporter's request, this report lists **all verifiable intervals of at least 30 seconds found in the available records**, including shorter cases, rather than selecting just the worst incidents. Some requests did complete promptly; this report focuses on the waits above that threshold. The threshold is the user's responsiveness expectation, not a published service SLA.

## Evidence and coverage
- Timestamped room messages were searched from the beginning of the accessible history; 31 create/update custom-rule card entries were found, dated October 12–14, 2026. Their surrounding requests and outcome messages were reviewed. Ten computer-use permission prompts were also found, but most lack a separately identifiable permission-request timestamp.
- The project's historical archives were checked as well. The archive review covered 506 distinct project messages beginning October 12 at 22:17 UTC. Its early snapshots explicitly disclose incomplete raw-transcript coverage. Some voice-era request text is absent from room history. A separate revision case on October 13 ran from the first card at 16:46:17.781 to the user's reported dismissal at 16:47:39.779 (**81.998 seconds**). This was human wording revision/dismissal time, not a saving failure or measured system delay; the replacement is listed separately above.

## Unanswered messages and coordination impact
- **October 13, 21:11–21:18:** a permanent-allowance request at 21:11:26 was followed by reminders at 21:13:13, 21:16:55 and 21:18:08 before the first assistant acknowledgment at 21:18:19 and card at 21:18:31.

The rule's saved result was reported at 21:35:21. Earlier approval timeouts were reported, but the assistant explicitly said they did not explain the later silence. A further approval-check timeout was reported at 21:40:51; the diagnostic finally ran by 21:44:31.
- **October 14, 03:34–03:43:** eight follow-ups appeared during the 8m16s request-to-card wait; the assistant said at 03:43:01 that the card had not yet been created.
- **October 14, 16:03–16:13:** after the card appeared, the user asked whether it saved at 16:04:11, 16:05:22, 16:05:38, 16:05:46 and 16:05:55. - **October 14, 17:41–18:08:** a requested card remained outstanding while the user repeated that they were waiting and then requested this bug report.

## Expected behavior
- Present a requested card promptly, or immediately expose an actionable blocker.
- Remain responsive to incoming user messages while a permission operation is pending.
- Continue independently authorized work and handoffs.
- Clearly expose whether the request has been dispatched, a card is ready, user action is pending, validation is running, or persistence succeeded/failed.
- Preserve pending requests through interruptions without silently dropping or duplicating them.
- Instrument request receipt, dispatch, card creation/render, user click, validation completion and outcome delivery separately.

Please investigate approval lifecycle and parent-agent dispatch/responsiveness together. This report does not establish intentional ignoring, a universal freeze, or the backend root cause, and does not ask to weaken permission checks.

items.title: macOS: custom permission profile blocks securityd XPC access required by Dataverse CLI

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1007.30912, build 20156.

Bundled runtime: `codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.17.2`.

### What subscription do you have?

Pro.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 26.7.1 (25G241), Apple Silicon.

Output of `uname -mprs`:

```text
Darwin 25.6.0 arm64 arm
```

### What issue are you seeing?

When Dataverse CLI runs inside Codex’s macOS sandbox with a custom permission profile, initialization of its encrypted token cache fails. The macOS sandbox log identifies a denied lookup of the Keychain-related XPC service:

```text
Sandbox: dataverse(87032) deny(1) mach-lookup com.apple.securityd.xpc
```

The command is a read-only identity request:

```sh
dataverse api request \
  --target dataverse \
  --path 'WhoAmI' \
  --method GET \
  --environment https://<development-environment>.crm4.dynamics.com/
```

It exits with code 1:

```text
warn: DataverseCli.Auth.PacAuthApplicationFactory[0]
Encrypted token cache not available, falling back to plaintext:
Persistence check failed. Reason: Could not create new item.
Error code: 100001. OS error code 100001.

ERROR: Value cannot be null. (Parameter 'keyChainServiceName')
```

Relevant stack frames:

```text
Microsoft.Identity.Client.Extensions.Msal.MacKeychainAccessor..ctor(...)
Microsoft.Identity.Client.Extensions.Msal.Storage.Create(...)
Microsoft.Identity.Client.Extensions.Msal.MsalCacheHelper.CreateAsync(...)
DataverseCli.Auth.PacAuthApplicationFactory.RegisterPlaintextCacheAsync(...)
DataverseCli.Auth.PacAuthApplicationFactory.RegisterTokenCacheAsync(...)
DataverseCli.Auth.PacAuthApplicationFactory.CreatePublicClientAsync(...)
DataverseCli.Auth.AuthTokenStore.AcquireTokenForEnvironmentAsync(...)
DataverseCli.Api.ApiCommand.RunRequestAsync(...)
```

The `keyChainServiceName` exception is a subsequent failure in Dataverse CLI’s fallback path. The Codex-specific problem reported here is the preceding sandbox denial of `com.apple.securityd.xpc`.

The custom profile already grants filesystem write access to:

```text
~/Library/Application Support/Microsoft/DataverseCli
~/Library/Application Support/Microsoft/PowerAppsCli
~/.local/share/Microsoft/PowerAppsCli
~/Library/Keychains
~/.net
```

Consequently, the command gets past the token-cache lockfile and .NET extraction stages, but still cannot complete the Keychain persistence check.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Install and authenticate `@microsoft/dataverse` on macOS. The tested npm package version is `1.0.82`.
2. Confirm that the identity request above succeeds in an ordinary Terminal.
3. Select a custom Codex permission profile that allows network access and writes to the CLI’s cache directories.
4. Ensure `DOTNET_BUNDLE_EXTRACT_BASE_DIR` points to an allowed writable directory.
5. Ask Codex to execute the identity request inside the sandbox.
6. Observe the persistence failure and the corresponding sandbox denial.
7. Run the same command outside the sandbox after approving escalation. It succeeds.

The following is a reduced illustration of the relevant effective permissions. It has not been tested independently as a minimal reproducer:

```toml
default_permissions = "dataverse-dev"
approval_policy = "on-request"

[shell_environment_policy.set]
DOTNET_BUNDLE_EXTRACT_BASE_DIR = "/Users/<user>/.net"

[permissions.dataverse-dev]
extends = ":workspace"

[permissions.dataverse-dev.filesystem]
"~/.net" = "write"
"~/Library/Application Support/Microsoft/DataverseCli" = "write"
"~/Library/Application Support/Microsoft/PowerAppsCli" = "write"
"~/.local/share/Microsoft/PowerAppsCli" = "write"
"~/Library/Keychains" = "write"

[permissions.dataverse-dev.network]
enabled = true
```

The relevant sandbox denial was also observed with PAC CLI:

```text
Sandbox: pac(87073) deny(1) mach-lookup com.apple.securityd.xpc
```

Escalation works in a newly started session configured with `on-request`; failure to display an approval request is not part of this report.

### What is the expected behavior?

Codex should provide a supported, explicitly opt-in way for a custom permission profile to allow the Keychain service access required by an authenticated CLI, while retaining its filesystem restrictions and macOS’s own per-item Keychain access controls.

If this service is intentionally unavailable to sandboxed commands, the restriction and the supported execution path should be documented clearly. Filesystem write permission for `~/Library/Keychains` does not resolve the denied XPC lookup.

### Additional information

Inspection of the installed desktop runtime found a sandbox allowance for `com.apple.SecurityServer`, but no occurrence of `com.apple.securityd.xpc`. This is consistent with the observed denial, although I have not modified the runtime or verified a patched build.

A candidate Seatbelt allowance to investigate is:

```scheme
(allow mach-lookup
  (global-name "com.apple.securityd.xpc"))
```

This is an implementation-level suggestion, not a supported `config.toml` setting or a verified complete fix.

Related reports:

- [#43610 — Support scoped credential-store writes for OAuth refresh by sandboxed CLIs](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/43610): similar Keychain write failure; this report adds the exact denied XPC service and a Dataverse/PAC reproduction.
- [#24742 — Support user-provided Seatbelt sandbox rules via config or drop-in file](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/24742): relevant to configuring a narrow service allowance.

No tokens, passwords, account identifiers, or actual environment URLs are included in this report.

items.title: Support store-owned preparation when resuming threads
items.body:
Support store-owned preparation when resuming threads

## Why

Thread stores need a way to reuse history and writer state loaded while preparing a resume, rather than loading them again during session startup.

## What changed

- Add an opaque, single-use `ThreadStoreResumePreparation` and an optional preparation in `StartThreadOptions`.
- Pass preparation through session startup to `ThreadStore::resume_thread_with_preparation`, which defaults to an unsupported-operation error.
- Reject preparation for ephemeral threads or threads without resumed history. Continue using `resume_thread` when no preparation is supplied.

## Testing

Add a regression test verifying that supplied preparation selects the prepared store path and propagates its unsupported-operation error instead of falling back to ordinary resume.

items.title: Coalesce overlapping native TLS root certificate loads
items.body:
Coalesce overlapping native TLS root certificate loads

## Why

Concurrent TLS client builds can independently load the same platform trust store. Share overlapping loads while preserving fresh trust reads for later builds.

## What changed

- Share one in-flight native root load without reusing completed loads.
- Bypass sharing when `SSL_CERT_FILE` or `SSL_CERT_DIR` is set, and continue reading custom CA bundles independently for every build.

## Testing

Add tests for overlapping loads, fresh trust after completion, and recovery from a panicking loader. Extend TLS handshake coverage to verify that replacing a custom CA file affects new configurations while existing configurations retain their trust, and that empty or removed files produce errors.

items.body:
Could you confirm whether an existing supported correction or version-specific contract addresses the cases below, and identify the applicable release, documentation, source change and regression evidence?

**Source reviewed:** commit `740e5af33c71225640e0c1c1555c514c2c93ab74`, associated with `rust-v0.162.0-alpha.17.2`. Scope: the Responses HTTP/WebSocket path, a fresh non-resumed single-turn `codex exec --json` invocation, its compaction paths and in-process App Server delivery. These are **source-supported paths, not live reproductions**. No runtime tests have been performed for this report. Independent build reproducibility and other bundled-component provenance are not established here.

The consumer problem is that successful model output and complete reported-usage coverage are different facts, but the terminal JSONL receipt exposes numeric usage without a completeness state. Zero may be legitimate when explicitly reported; nonzero may be partial. Neither value alone establishes coverage. This request concerns reported checkpoint accounting, not provider billing finality, a hard token cap or interception before every internal request.

## Findings

| Finding and triggering conditions | Resulting receipt behavior and consumer impact | Immutable source locations |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Missing usage:** a provider completion omits its optional usage object. Ordinary sampling still succeeds. | The history accumulator is unchanged and no incomplete-coverage state is recorded. With no cached total, CLI completion uses default zeros; after an earlier reported response, it can use that unchanged subtotal. A consumer cannot distinguish known zero/full coverage from missing or partial accounting. | [Optional provider usage][provider]; [recording skips absent usage][record]; [sampling success][sampling]; [notification suppression and success mapping][mapping]; [CLI default][cache]; [terminal projection][terminal]. |
| **Delivery asymmetry:** the bounded in-process event queue is full when a usage update is emitted. | Usage notifications are outside the required-delivery set and can be dropped by `try_send`; completion instead awaits delivery. Successful completion can therefore arrive with an absent or stale CLI cache. The drop branch logs without emitting a typed accounting-invalid marker. Producer ordering alone does not establish terminal coverage. | [Required-delivery classification][delivery]; [drop versus awaited delivery][drop]; [CLI cache/completion][terminal]. |
| **Remote-v2 compaction divergence:** that compaction branch completes with reported usage. | The raw completion and separate usage record retain the report, while the successful remote-v2 path updates rollout budget/analytics and recomputes context without adding that usage to the history cumulative total used by CLI completion. The CLI subtotal can omit reported compaction usage. Local summarizing compaction takes a different accumulation path. | [Branch selection][selection]; [remote-v2 budget/context path and collector][remote]; [separate reported record][record]; [local accumulation][local]; [CLI total projection][cache]. |
| **Synthetic context accounting:** context-window-exceeded handling fills usage to the context window; context recomputation also runs during context replacement. | Synthetic fill replaces cumulative `total_tokens` with the context-window value and defaults input/output/detail fields to zero. Recompute separately changes **last** usage to an estimated context total, preserving cumulative usage or initializing it to zero; it does not directly insert that estimate into CLI input/output totals. Shared state therefore mixes accounting purposes. Ordinary sampling failure is an error, but optional post-turn compaction failure can preserve completed output after such mutation. | [Synthetic replacement][fill]; [sampling error caller][sampling-error]; [local compaction error caller][compact-error]; [recompute][estimate]; [post-turn failure handling][post-turn]. |
| **Retry/replay coverage remains unresolved:** a stream fails before a completion report, then a retry/reconnect succeeds; or a response might be replayed. | Received completion reports are added, but the inspected path does not recover missing reports or mark their coverage unresolved. Addition has no response-ID deduplication; each stream stops at its first completion, which does not establish cross-retry exactly-once semantics. Whether a later provider report covers an earlier failed request, or a replay repeats the same usage, remains unconfirmed provider semantics. No omitted amount or actual duplicate is asserted. | [Retry loop][retry]; [fallback and retry policy][retry-policy]; [element-wise addition][addition]; [stream completion boundary][websocket]. |
| **Delegated agents are separate:** an invocation creates child threads. | Root CLI notification filtering accepts only its selected thread/turn; it is not an agent-tree usage aggregate. Forked children can inherit prior usage state, so their own cumulative figures need a baseline. Consumers must not infer descendant coverage from a root receipt or shared session identity. | [Child creation][children]; [root identity filter][filter]; [resume/fork usage restoration][history]. |

These findings establish code behavior and conditional paths. Live provider omission frequency, actual queue saturation, active compaction configuration, replay behavior and end-to-end receipt correctness have not been observed. In particular, the retry/replay question is unresolved rather than a confirmed provider accounting defect.

## Requested supported terminal accounting contract

Please identify an existing contract/correction, or provide a supported terminal result with these properties; field names and implementation are open:

1. **Identity and interval:** bind accounting to execution/attempt, thread and turn identities, define start/end boundaries and baseline, and declare whether totals cover the root thread or an explicitly defined aggregate. Explain resume/fork boundaries and separately scoped delegated usage.
2. **Reported subtotal and coverage:** preserve received reported input/output subtotals separately from coverage status and unresolved reasons. Distinguish model success from accounting complete/incomplete/unknown. Missing usage must not become known zero, and a new notification containing an old total must not certify fresh coverage. State defaults for optional detail fields and distinguish them from reported values.
3. **Authoritative terminal result:** preserve terminal accounting despite intermediate usage-notification loss, through an authoritative terminal snapshot or equivalent supported mechanism. Define its ordering and retrieval/delivery behavior; absence of an authoritative result remains unresolved. Success alone must not certify a cached subtotal.
4. **Compaction and estimates:** include each supported summarizing compaction report exactly once within the declared scope, without duplicating existing rollout-budget charges. Keep reported cumulative usage independent of context estimates, context-window fills and context resets. A context-only reset creates no synthetic provider consumption.
5. **Retry/replay:** define report/request identities, scope, duplicate and conflict handling, and whether a later report covers an earlier failed request. Preserve unresolved coverage after lost completion, interruption or ambiguous restart unless supported recovery evidence resolves it. Locally assigned timestamps/sequences cannot establish provider-report completeness.

## Focused correction acceptance scenarios

These are requested acceptance criteria, not tests run or results claimed here. Illustrative token values are synthetic fixtures.

| Scenario | Required observable outcome |
| --- | --- |
| **Positive ordinary path:** two root-thread responses, including a tool follow-up, report 100/10 and 30/4 input/output. | Terminal subtotal is 130/14, attributed to the exact declared interval; coverage is complete only under the supported report-coverage contract. Model outcome is represented independently. |
| **First-response missing usage:** model output completes without a usage object. | Model success remains representable; accounting explicitly records no report/incomplete coverage. Complete actual usage remains unknown, rather than certified numeric zero. An explicitly reported all-zero usage case remains distinguishable and is not rejected merely for being zero. |
| **Later-response missing usage:** first response reports 100/10; a follow-up completes without usage. | Preserve 100/10 as the reported partial subtotal and identify incomplete coverage. Re-emitting that subtotal must not make it complete. |
| **Queue saturation:** newest usage update is dropped while terminal completion survives. | Terminal accounting still supplies the authoritative latest result and coverage state, or explicitly reports incompleteness. It must not label an absent/stale cache complete. Test loss of the first and of a later update. |
| **Compaction:** exercise local summarizing and remote-v2 paths with present and missing usage; exercise token-budget context-only reset. | Every present summarizing report contributes once to the declared reported subtotal; missing reports mark coverage incomplete. Existing budget charges occur once. Context-only reset adds no reported model usage. |
| **Synthetic reset:** force context recompute and context-window fill after a known subtotal, including optional post-turn compaction failure that preserves output. | Known reported subtotal is preserved independently of estimates/fills; accounting uncertainty is explicit. Successful output cannot hide zeroed/reset reported fields. |
| **Retry/replay ambiguity:** failed stream before completion followed by success; identical response replay; conflicting usage for the same identity. | Define covered and unresolved requests. Identical replay counts once under supported identity semantics; conflicting evidence remains unresolved without silently replacing totals. Later success does not erase earlier uncertainty absent authoritative recovery. |
| **Delegation/baseline:** root plus child reports, and a child fork with inherited usage. | Root scope and child scope are explicit; inherited baseline is not fresh child consumption. Any aggregate is documented and counts each scoped report once. |

Please supply the precise supported scope and version, the upstream explanation of retry/replay coverage, and regression evidence connecting authoritative terminal accounting to these scenarios. If existing behavior intentionally exposes only a best-effort subtotal, please document that limitation and its missing/reset/loss signals so consumers can retain UNKNOWN accounting instead of interpreting a successful receipt as complete.

Accounting completeness does not establish operating-system process/descendant closure or permission for subsequent execution.

items.body: Codex macOS **26.1007.71326**, build **20398**. After updating, a long conversation jumps from yesterday at 8:39 p.m. straight to today at 9:24 p.m. Four completed turns covering most of today’s work are missing from the UI. Screenshot attached. The missing turns are present in the saved transcript, history database, and thread-read API. I traced a likely cause in the bundled history loader: it fetches five turns but shares a 500-item budget across them. The newest turn has 542 items and exhausts that budget. items.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

0.162.1

### What subscription do you have?

Bedrock

### Which model were you using?

GPT-5.6 Sol (Global)

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 5.10.269-278.1108.amzn2int.x86_64 x86_64 x86_64

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

Ghostty

### Codex doctor report

```json

```

### What issue are you seeing?

## Environment

- Codex CLI: `0.162.1`
- Approval reviewer: `auto_review`
- Multi-agent session containing encrypted `agent_message` items

## Description

After a Guardian review admits an encrypted parent `agent_message`, a model
failure can leave the reviewer session reusable without advancing its
transcript-admission cursor. The next approval review reuses the mutated
Guardian thread, selects the full transcript again, and appends the same native
message with the same `amsg_…` ID.

The subsequent Responses request contains the ID twice and fails before the
requested action runs:

```text
Duplicate item found with id amsg_<redacted>.
Remove duplicate items from your input and try again.
```

In the observed sequence, the initiating Guardian failure was:

```text
Encrypted content cannot be used in a different region from the one that created it.
```

The cross-region failure triggers this instance, but the persistent
duplicate-ID state is caused locally by retaining the failed reviewer while its
history and transcript cursor disagree.

## Expected behavior

A reusable Guardian session should never admit the same native response-item ID
twice. A review that reaches authoritative `TurnComplete` should advance live
transcript-admission progress even when it does not produce a successful
assessment. Successful-review counters and committed checkpoints should remain
success-only.

## Actual behavior

1. The Guardian context clones encrypted `agent_message` evidence with its
   original `amsg_…` ID.
2. Final input admission records it in the Guardian thread.
3. The model turn reaches `TurnComplete` with an error.
4. The reviewer is retained as reusable.
5. The transcript cursor is not advanced because the outcome is
   `SessionFailed`, not `Completed`.
6. The next review admits the full transcript into the same thread and
   duplicates the ID.

## Source analysis

- Encrypted native messages retain their IDs:
  [`[guardian-context/src/transcript.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/76ed3b484d62ccceb9fa512ff4dd139f421814c3/codex-rs/guardian-context/src/transcript.rs#L183-L209)`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/76ed3b484d62ccceb9fa512ff4dd139f421814c3/codex-rs/guardian-context/src/transcript.rs#L183-L209)
- Final admission preserves native message identity:
  [`[core/src/guardian/input_budget.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/76ed3b484d62ccceb9fa512ff4dd139f421814c3/codex-rs/core/src/guardian/input_budget.rs#L261-L307)`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/76ed3b484d62ccceb9fa512ff4dd139f421814c3/codex-rs/core/src/guardian/input_budget.rs#L261-L307)
- A completed error returns a reusable reviewer:
  [`[guardian-reviewer/src/execution.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/76ed3b484d62ccceb9fa512ff4dd139f421814c3/codex-rs/ext/guardian-reviewer/src/execution.rs#L116-L136)`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/76ed3b484d62ccceb9fa512ff4dd139f421814c3/codex-rs/ext/guardian-reviewer/src/execution.rs#L116-L136)
- Transcript progress advances only for `Completed`:
  [`[core/src/guardian/review_session.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/76ed3b484d62ccceb9fa512ff4dd139f421814c3/codex-rs/core/src/guardian/review_session.rs#L799-L828)`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/76ed3b484d62ccceb9fa512ff4dd139f421814c3/codex-rs/core/src/guardian/review_session.rs#L799-L828)
- `ConversationState::complete_review` combines cursor advancement with the
  successful-review count:
  [`[guardian-reviewer/src/conversation.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/76ed3b484d62ccceb9fa512ff4dd139f421814c3/codex-rs/ext/guardian-reviewer/src/conversation.rs#L51-L69)`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/76ed3b484d62ccceb9fa512ff4dd139f421814c3/codex-rs/ext/guardian-reviewer/src/conversation.rs#L51-L69)

The ID-bearing Guardian behavior was introduced by
[[#49038](https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/49038)](https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/49038). Its regression test covers
successful incremental reviews, but not a failed review followed by reuse.

## Proposed fix

- Separate transcript admission from successful-review completion in
  `ConversationState`.
- When a reusable review reaches authoritative `TurnComplete`, advance its live
  transcript cursor and source/version state.
- Increment `completed_review_count` only for a successful `Completed`
  assessment.
- At final native-message admission, suppress an item whose ID is already in
  the effective reviewer history.
- Add a regression scenario:
  - admit one encrypted `agent_message`;
  - fail the first Guardian inference;
  - reuse the reviewer;
  - assert the second wire request contains the original `amsg_…` ID exactly
    once.

## Related issue

[[#15608](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/15608)](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/15608) reports the same server
validation text through a different WebSocket seed-context duplication path.
This report concerns Guardian transcript admission after a failed reusable
review.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

See the description above (reproducibility is not deterministic and not user driven)

### What is the expected behavior?

A reusable Guardian session should never admit the same native response-item ID
twice. A review that reaches authoritative `TurnComplete` should advance live
transcript-admission progress even when it does not produce a successful
assessment. Successful-review counters and committed checkpoints should remain
success-only.

### Additional information

items.body:
> Disclosure: OpenAI Codex performed the local investigation and diagnostic tests described below, and drafted and submitted this report through my GitHub account at my request.

## Summary
On Windows, `codex resume "<session-name>"` reports that no saved session exists even though the name is present in both `session_index.jsonl` and `state_5.sqlite`, and `thread/list` and `thread/read` return the correct named thread.

The affected thread has a Windows verbatim path (`\\?\C:\...`) stored in `threads.rollout_path`. Name lookup rejects that path when checking whether it starts with the non-verbatim sessions root. Resume by UUID succeeds.

## Environment
- Codex CLI: `0.162.1`, installed through npm
- OS: Windows Server 2025, build 26100, x64
- Shell: PowerShell
- Affected session originally created with CLI `0.153.4`
- Session source: `cli`; not archived; model provider: `openai`
- API reported history mode: `paginated`

## Steps to reproduce
1. On Windows, create a session and rename it using `/rename kex`.
2. Close and resume the session by UUID. In the tested environment, opening the session stores `threads.rollout_path` with a `\\?\` prefix.
3. Exit and run `codex resume kex` from the saved project directory.
4. Observe:
   ```text
   No saved session found with ID kex. Run `codex resume` without an ID to choose from existing sessions.
   ```
5. Run `codex resume <SESSION_UUID>`: the same conversation opens successfully.

The original reproduction used an existing session created on 0.153.4, rather than a clean new-session test on 0.162.1.

## Expected behavior
Resume by the exact name saved through `/rename` should open the same session as resume by UUID. Equivalent Windows paths should pass the local sessions-root check.

## Diagnostic evidence
- `session_index.jsonl` contains the expected `thread_name`.
- SQLite `threads.name` contains the same name; `archived = 0`.
- `thread/list` with active CLI/VSCode sources includes the affected thread and correct name.
- `thread/read` by UUID returns the same correct name and path.
- The rollout file exists and the session opens successfully by UUID.
- `--all` does not fix name lookup.
- `--no-daemon` does not fix name lookup.
- Temporarily removing only the `\\?\` prefix from that thread's SQLite `rollout_path` makes `codex resume kex` succeed.
- Opening the session writes the prefixed path back, so that database edit is not a persistent workaround.

No conversation content or private project data is included in this report. Paths below use placeholders:
```text
Stored rollout_path: \\?\C:\Users\<user>\.codex\sessions\...\rollout-<session>.jsonl
Expected root:       C:\Users\<user>\.codex\sessions
```

## Suspected root cause
In `codex-rs/tui/src/named_session_lookup.rs` at tag `rust-v0.162.1`, local named-session lookup skips a candidate when:
```rust
!path.starts_with(expected_root)
```
The stored verbatim path and the non-verbatim sessions root represent the same location, but have different Windows path prefixes. The controlled SQLite-path test above points to this check as the cause.

Source: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.1/codex-rs/tui/src/named_session_lookup.rs

## Suggested fix
Normalize both paths to a consistent Windows representation before the containment check, while preserving the intended sessions-root containment restriction. Also keep persisted rollout paths consistent across resume operations.

A regression test should verify that the named-session lookup accepts a verbatim rollout path inside the equivalent non-verbatim sessions root, still rejects paths outside the root, and continues working after reopening the session.

## Workaround
Use `codex resume <SESSION_UUID>`.

## Related reports
- #39239: archive failure after resume persists a verbatim rollout path; a similar controlled prefix-removal test, but a different failing code path.
- #26059: stale-path mismatch while resuming a running thread; a different error from the name-lookup failure reported here.

After restarting internal Codex processes, the model became available, but submitting a message still froze the interface and conversations still did not load.

Closing and reopening the app window did not fix the problem. With the window closed, PowerShell still showed **19 `ChatGPT.exe` processes and 2 `codex.exe` processes** running.

This has happened repeatedly after Codex Desktop updates on this Windows machine. The exact trigger and root cause have not been isolated.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

These are the steps observed during the October 14 incident; the failure is recurring but is not confirmed to occur after every update:

1. Update the Microsoft Store Codex Desktop app to version 26.1007.9446.0 and launch it on Windows 11 x64.
2. Open an existing local conversation and a conversation created on another device. Their contents do not load.
3. Create a new conversation. The model selector initially shows `Loading model`.
4. Restart the internal Codex processes. The model selector then shows an available model, but opening conversations and submitting a message still fail or freeze the interface.
5. Close the app window and reopen it. The problem persists.
6. Close the window again and inspect processes in PowerShell. In this incident, 19 `ChatGPT.exe` and 2 `codex.exe` processes remained active.

No private session IDs or project details are included in this public report.

### What is the expected behavior?

Existing conversations should load after an update, and a new conversation should initialize a model and accept messages without freezing. Closing the application should not leave processes in a state that prevents a normal relaunch.

### Additional information

- `Test-NetConnection api.openai.com -Port 443` returned `True`. This confirms TCP connectivity to that host and port, but does not establish that all application services were reachable.
- **Successful recovery:** Terminating only the remaining processes whose executable paths belonged to OpenAI Codex, then reopening the app, restored conversations and their context. No app data was deleted and no reinstall was needed.
- **Hypothesis, not confirmed cause:** A stale or hung background process after updating may interfere with app startup or session loading. The process counts and recovery above are observations; they do not by themselves establish the underlying defect.

items.body:
# Bug report: the in-app browser never binds to the active conversation, and the Chrome/Edge native-host runtime registry is never written

## Environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| OS | Windows 11 Home China, 10.0.26200, x64, locale zh-CN |
| Codex desktop app | 26.1007.9446.0 (Store package `OpenAI.Codex_..._2p2nqsd0c76g0`) |
| Codex CLI | 0.162.1 (standalone install) |
| Bundled plugins | browser / chrome / computer-use all 26.1007.71326, installed + enabled |
| CODEX_HOME | `C:\Users\<user>\.codex`, which is a **symlink** to `D:\Codex\.codex` |
| Default browser | Microsoft Edge |
| Extension | `hehggadaopoacecdllhhajmbjkdcmajg` installed + enabled in both Chrome and Edge (Default profile) |

Relevant feature flags (`codex features list`) are all enabled: `browser_use`,
`browser_use_external`, `computer_use`, `in_app_browser`.

The app's own availability state machine resolves to the success state:

    browser_use_availability_resolved available=true browserPane=true
      platform=Windows reason=available release=26.1007.71326

So this is not a gating / entitlement / settings problem. Decoded from `app.asar`, the
other possible reasons would have been `statsig-disabled`, `browser-pane-disabled`,
`config-requirement-disabled` or `wsl-disabled`. None of those is reported.

---

## Issue 1 - the in-app browser route is reassigned to an unsent "new chat" draft

`agent.browsers.get("iab")` fails in the conversation the user is actually typing in.
Two distinct failure modes are observed.

### 1a. Route stolen by a `client-new-thread:` draft

Every attempt produces this sequence in the desktop app log. The route is taken from the
real conversation and handed to an unsent new-chat draft:

    IAB_LIFECYCLE received browser sidebar owner sync
        conversationId=client-new-thread:85bc1bb7-280d-41ea-9429-566756fd062f
    IAB_LIFECYCLE reassigned browser use route
        sourceConversationId=01a13b39-24c2-7ef0-9407-9aab3d8b8f06   <- the real conversation
        targetConversationId=client-new-thread:85bc1bb7-280d-41ea-9429-566756fd062f
    IAB_LIFECYCLE iab backend info request failed
        conversationId=01a13b39-24c2-7ef0-9407-9aab3d8b8f06
        errorMessage="No ChatGPT browser route is available for browser session 01a13b39-..."
    IAB_LIFECYCLE created browser use host
        conversationId=client-new-thread:85bc1bb7-...
        routeKey=1:client-new-thread:85bc1bb7-...
    IAB_LIFECYCLE ended browser use session activity
        conversationId=01a13b39-24c2-7ef0-9407-9aab3d8b8f06

The same pattern repeats with different draft ids (`c5896cf5`, `60c87272`, `967bcc59`,
`766a9dc0`, `85bc1bb7`): each time the app creates a fresh draft, the draft takes the pane.

Some `getInfo` calls for the same conversation *succeed* while adjacent ones fail, so the
binding is also flapping:

    iab backend info request completed  conversationId=01a13b39-...  metadataCodexSessionId=01a13b39-...
    iab backend info request failed     conversationId=01a13b39-...  "No ChatGPT browser route is available"

### 1b. `iab` absent from `browsers.list()` entirely

In other attempts no iab backend is started for the new conversation at all, and the agent
gets:

    Browser is not available: iab

In one session this was called 23 times, all of them *before* the app started an iab
backend for that conversation. The backend only became ready about 2.5 hours later, when
the browser sidebar happened to be bound to it.

### What was tried, with no effect

- Sending a message first so the conversation has a real id, *then* opening the Browser pane
- Opening the Browser pane first, then asking
- Loading a real page in the pane rather than leaving it blank
- Using the documented `[@Browser](plugin://browser@openai-bundled)` plugin mention
- Reducing to a single app window (logs had shown both `windowId=1` and `windowId=3`)
- Reinstalling the Browser plugin from the app's plugin UI
- Restarting the app repeatedly

The provider side is healthy throughout: `browser_use_iab_backend_startup_ready` is logged
with a pipe path, and all `\\.\pipe\codex-browser-use*` pipes accept connections (verified
by connecting to all 14 of them directly). The failure is purely the
`(windowId, conversationId)` route binding.

---

## Issue 2 - `chrome-native-hosts-v2.json` is never rewritten, so Computer Use cannot read a browser URL

`%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI\Codex\chrome-native-hosts-v2.json` is the runtime registry that
`extension-host.exe` reads to find a live Codex runtime. Both `app.asar` and
`extension-host.exe` contain that filename; `codex.exe` does not, so only the desktop app
writes it.

On this machine its single entry is stale, last written 2026-10-14 09:54 local:

    appVersion : 26.1007.21434
    entryId    : codex-runtime-b097ad1c296eb4c397931a8d229997df
    presence   : pid 19348, lastSeenAt 2026-10-14T01:53:36Z
    extensionHostPath : C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\OpenAI.Codex_26.1007.2314.0_x64__2p2nqsd0c76g0\...\extension-host.exe
    browserClientPath : C:\Users\<user>\.codex\plugins\cache\openai-bundled\chrome\latest\scripts\browser-client.mjs

Problems with that entry:

1. `presence.pid` 19348 is **dead**.
2. `extensionHostPath` points into app package **26.1007.2314.0**, which the update to
   26.1007.9446.0 removed, so the path **does not resolve**.
3. `browserClientPath` references `...\chrome\latest\scripts\`, but nothing creates the
   `latest` junction (see secondary findings), and since 26.1007.71326 the chrome plugin
   ships no `scripts/` directory at all.

### The app never rewrites it

- Restarting the app 4+ times, including after the update to 26.1007.9446.0: file untouched.
- **Deleting the file and restarting the app: it is not recreated.**
- Reinstalling the Browser plugin from the app's plugin UI: it is not recreated.
- Across every desktop log on this machine, the strings `chrome-native-hosts`,
  `codex-runtime-`, `entryId`, `installId` and `nativeHostVersion` have **zero** hits, so
  the write path is silent and apparently never runs.

`extension-host.exe` processes *do* start when Chrome or Edge launches (confirmed by
process start times matching browser launches), so the Chrome/Edge side of native
messaging works. The host simply has no live runtime to connect to.

### Observable consequence: Computer Use is hard-blocked on all browser windows

Computer Use itself is healthy. `sky.list_windows()` returns windows, and screenshots,
clicks and accessibility trees all work on non-browser apps. But any interaction with a
browser window fails with:

    Computer Use has been stopped for this turn because it could not determine the current
    browser URL on Windows with enough confidence to enforce policy. Stop your work and
    send a final message noting why Computer Use ended.

(from `src/policy/url_policy.rs` in `codex-computer-use.exe`; this is the "supported
browser, URL unreadable" variant, not the "browser not supported" variant.) Since the
policy check needs the extension to report the URL, and the extension has no route to a
live runtime, every browser task is refused. This makes Computer Use unusable for web work.

---

## Secondary findings (genuine gaps, worked around locally)

1. **`plugins\cache\openai-bundled\chrome\latest` is never created.**
   The runtime registry references `...\chrome\latest\scripts\browser-client.mjs` and
   `browser-service.mjs`, but `codex plugin add` only copies files and creates no junction,
   and no plugin directory on this machine ever had a `latest` entry. After an update the
   junction also goes stale. Creating it by hand makes those paths resolve.

2. **The Edge NativeMessagingHosts registry root is never written.**
   `installManifest.mjs` registers only `HKCU\Software\Google\Chrome\NativeMessagingHosts`,
   but Edge reads `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Edge\NativeMessagingHosts`. With the extension
   installed and enabled in Edge, it could never reach the native host. Adding the Edge key
   made Edge spawn `extension-host.exe` on launch. For comparison, another vendor's
   extension on this machine registers under both roots.

3. **`codex plugin remove/add` does no wiring.**
   It does not create `latest`, does not write `extension-host-config.json`, does not touch
   the manifest, and does not refresh the runtime registry. Worth documenting, because
   `docs/chrome-troubleshooting.md` tells users to reinstall the Browser plugin - but the
   app UI reinstall did not refresh the registry either.

4. **A symlinked `CODEX_HOME` breaks `.mjs` MCP servers.**
   With `C:\Users\<user>\.codex` symlinked to `D:\Codex\.codex`, Node resolves
   `import.meta.url` to the real path (`file:///D:/...`) while
   `pathToFileURL(process.argv[1])` keeps `file:///C:/...`. The common main-module guard

       if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href) await runStdio();

   is therefore never true, the server exits 0 without serving, and Codex reports
   `MCP server startup failed: connection closed: initialize response`. Resolving the
   configured path through the symlink, or comparing real paths, would avoid this.

---

## Elimination tests (both negative) - please do not re-suggest these

### A stale runtime registry is NOT the (only) cause of the Computer Use block

To rule out the stale registry, `chrome-native-hosts-v2.json` was rewritten by hand with
fully valid, live values, taken from the app's own log line
`browser_use_runtime_paths_selected`:

    appVersion / cliVersion / nativeHostVersion = 26.1007.71326
    presence.pid       = the live desktop app main process (verified ALIVE)
    presence.*         = current timestamps
    codexCliPath       = ...\OpenAI\Codex\bin\9614f1d9b40d9c4f\codex.exe
    nodePath           = ...\runtimes\cua_node\a9ba6825a525118c\bin\node.exe
    nodeReplPath       = ...\runtimes\cua_node\a9ba6825a525118c\bin\node_repl.exe
    nodeModuleDirs[0]  = ...\runtimes\cua_node\a9ba6825a525118c\bin\node_modules
    extensionHostPath  = <current 26.1007.9446.0 package>\...\extension-host.exe
    browserClientPath  = ...\browser\26.1007.71326\scripts\browser-client.mjs
    browserServicePath = ...\browser\26.1007.71326\scripts\browser-service.mjs

All nine paths were verified to resolve, and the pid was verified alive at test time.
Chrome and Edge were then both fully restarted, and three `extension-host.exe` processes
spawned and stayed alive.

**Computer Use still fails with the identical error.** So the browser URL cannot be
determined even with a valid, live registry entry and a working native-messaging
transport. Something else in the URL-determination path is failing.

(Note: the registry has since been restored to the original app-written content, so the
machine reflects the real defect rather than the synthetic test entry.)

### The "keep the pane bound to an existing conversation" workaround does NOT fix iab

Derived from `ownerRoutePath` in the logs, the sidebar owner follows whatever page the
window is currently displaying:

    ownerRoutePath=/local/01a137a8-...        -> route bound to that conversation
    ownerRoutePath=/settings/plugins-settings -> route rebound to a client-new-thread draft
    ownerRoutePath=/settings/browser-use      -> route rebound to a client-new-thread draft
    ownerRoutePath=/                          -> route rebound to a client-new-thread draft

So the test was repeated in an **existing** conversation, in a single window, without ever
opening a new chat or a settings page, with a real page loaded in the pane first.

**`agent.browsers.get("iab")` still returns `Browser is not available: iab`.**

## What would help

- **Issue 1:** do not let a `client-new-thread:` draft take the browser route away from a
  conversation that is requesting it, or expose a way to pin the pane to the active
  conversation.
- **Issue 2:** make the desktop app rewrite `chrome-native-hosts-v2.json` on startup, and
  at minimum when the file is missing or when its `extensionHostPath` no longer resolves
  after an app update. Note from the elimination test above that this alone is unlikely to
  be sufficient for the Computer Use URL check - that path appears to have a second defect.
- **Diagnostics:** the URL-determination failure in `url_policy.rs` reports only
  "could not determine ... with enough confidence". Logging which source was consulted
  (extension channel, UI Automation, CDP) and why it was rejected would make this
  self-serviceable.

### Summary

Attached GitHub pull requests show 404 in the desktop app's native PR review view even though the same pull requests are accessible through the GitHub connector and Codex's CI-check tool. The user reports the failure across multiple pull requests.

### Environment

- Desktop app: ChatGPT 26.1007.71326, build 20398 (Codex workspace).
- macOS 27.0.1, build 26A434.
- Observed on October 14, 2026.
- Two GitHub accounts are configured. Diagnostic reads explicitly selected the account authorized for the affected repository.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a local repository task in the desktop app's Codex workspace.
2. Attach a valid GitHub pull request with `attach_artifact(artifact_type="pull_request", url=<canonical PR URL>)`.
3. Open the attached PR in the native review view.
4. Observe 404 instead of the PR metadata and diff.
5. Remove and reattach the PR, then open it again: the failure persists.

### Actual behavior and diagnostics

- The user sees 404 inside the desktop app; removing and reattaching repeatedly does not resolve it.
- `attach_artifact` succeeds, and `list_artifacts` returns a `pull_request` entry with the correct URL and GitHub identity.
- The attachment payload contains `root: null` and `headBranch: null`. This is an observation, not an established cause.
- The GitHub connector's `get_pr_info` successfully reads the same open, non-draft PR. Codex's `pull_requests_checks`, explicitly selecting the authorized account, also successfully retrieves its CI checks.
- `open_in_codex` accepts a PR review link with a file path and positive line number and returns `status: "queued"`, but the user still reports 404 in the review UI.

### Expected behavior

The native PR review view resolves an attached, accessible GitHub pull request and displays its metadata and diff. If that view requires a different authorization context, it should explain the required connection rather than present an unexplained 404.

### Privacy and limits

Private repository names, PR URLs, source code, account identifiers, session transcripts, and raw logs are omitted. The UI error is user-reported; agent diagnostics verify successful attachment registration and successful API reads. The underlying failing HTTP endpoint and root cause have not been identified.

Bound concurrent Git diffs for untracked files

## Why

Collecting a diff previously launched a Git process for every untracked file at once, allowing process counts to grow with the number of files.

Limit untracked-file diffs to eight concurrent operations per collection while preserving patch order and skipping failed file diffs. Concurrent collections each retain their own limit.

Add tests for independent concurrency limits, failed-file handling, and patch order and application with tracked changes, binary files, and filenames containing spaces or a leading dash.

labels.name: bug

items.body:
## Environment

- Windows 10 Pro x64, build 19045.
- ChatGPT sign-in (no API key used).
- App About version reported by the user: 26.1007.21434, released October 8, 2026.
- Installed desktop package version subsequently reported by `codex doctor`: 26.1007.9446.0. These are separate version sources; their relationship has not been established.
- Bundled runtime: 0.162.0-alpha.17.2.
- Selected and persisted model: `gpt-6.1-sol`, reasoning effort `medium`.
- Observed October 14, 2026.

## Problem

Two existing desktop chats cannot continue after switching from GPT-5.5 to GPT-6.1 Sol. The picker shows GPT-6.1 Sol, but the next message triggers pre-turn compaction and fails with:

```text
The 'gpt-5.5' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account.
Error running remote compact task: ... HTTP 400 invalid_request_error ...
```

The user corrected the user-level default to `model = "gpt-6.1-sol"`, saved it, restarted the app, and rebooted Windows. The failure persisted. Read-only inspection confirms both affected chats' stored model is also `gpt-6.1-sol`.

## Diagnostic evidence

At 2026-10-14 16:23:33 UTC (12:23:33 EDT), the affected turn's logs show:

```text
model=gpt-6.1-sol codex.turn.reasoning_effort=medium
run_auto_compact{reason=CompHashChanged phase=PreTurn}
previous-model compaction failed; retried with current model
previous_model="gpt-5.5"
current_model="gpt-6.1-sol"
reason=CompHashChanged
implementation=ResponsesCompactionV2
outcome="failed"
fallback_error=Some(Stream("stream closed before response.completed", None))
Failed to run pre-sampling compact
```

The same turn also records compaction retry warnings:

```text
compact_error=We're currently experiencing high demand, which may cause temporary errors.
compact_error=stream disconnected before completion: stream closed before response.completed
retries=2 max_retries=2
```

The high-demand warning is an observation, not a proven explanation for the fallback failure.

The GPT-6.1 Sol fallback received HTTP 200 from the Responses endpoint, but the stream did not complete. Request IDs from two fallback attempts:
- `286bfd09-ea41-435b-8f0a-06c720f932db`
- `7c065826-a518-4554-8aca-d02a451a3a65`

The chat UI/recorded final turn error still reports the original unsupported GPT-5.5 error.

A diagnostic run under the actual Windows user account confirms:
- user configuration parses and resolves to GPT-6.1 Sol;
- ChatGPT auth is configured;
- HTTP endpoint reachability and WebSocket handshake pass;
- state, log, and history database integrity checks pass.

These checks do not establish that streamed compaction requests succeed.

## Reproduction observed

1. Open an existing desktop chat with previous GPT-5.5 history.
2. Select GPT-6.1 Sol.
3. Send a new message.
4. Pre-turn compaction runs for CompHashChanged.
5. Previous-model compaction fails; current-model fallback also fails.
6. The turn stops and the UI displays the obsolete model's unsupported error.
7. Retrying after correcting the default and rebooting produces the same failure.

No minimal synthetic reproduction has been run.

## Expected behavior

A chat switched to a supported model should recover through compaction. If fallback fails, the final error should identify the current-model failure as well as the original failure, so users are not led to repeatedly change an already-correct model setting.

Please advise on a supported way to recover the existing histories without deleting turns or editing databases.

## Recovery investigation

The documented app-server API successfully exported the affected chat's history. A separate app-server process could not resume it because the desktop app owns the writer lock (`already has an active writer`). No compaction or direct database modifications were made by that recovery attempt. Manual `/compact` in the owning desktop app was subsequently tested; see the result below.

Related, but different failures:
- #32453: previous-model compaction blocked by HTTP 429.
- #48949: previous-model compaction across compatibility hashes on Bedrock.

No transcripts, credentials, repository contents, or unfiltered logs are included in this report.

## Manual-compaction result (October 14, 2026)

The user ran the desktop app's `/compact` command at 16:37:36 UTC (12:37:36 EDT). Local logs confirm this was `op.dispatch.compact` / `session_task.compact`, explicitly using `model=gpt-6.1-sol` and reasoning effort `medium`. It failed at 16:37:40 UTC after the two retry warnings, with:

```text
Error running remote compact task: stream disconnected before completion: stream closed before response.completed
```

This verifies that manual compaction with the current model also fails, independently of the initial previous-model rejection. The reason the stream closes is still unknown. No successful recovery has been established.
